hints: The total sum must be even before it can be split equally.
The target subset sum is half the total; counting subsets of this sum counts each partition twice, once per side.
Use one-dimensional subset-sum counting and divide by two modulo the required modulus.
analogy: Count all ways to choose one half; each balanced division appears again when the other half is chosen.
example: For n=3, {1,2,3} has total 6; subsets summing to 3 are {3} and {1,2}, representing the same split, so answer 1.
algorithm: Set dp[0]=1 and process values 1..n with descending sums up to total/2. The answer is dp[target]*inverse(2) modulo 1,000,000,007; use modular inverse because the modulus is prime.
correctness: Every equal partition contributes exactly two target-sum subsets, complementary sides; halving the subset count yields each unordered partition once.
